questions.prompt: What is a reliable compiler-version migration approach?
options: Assume old compiler options and tooling always remain supported.
Publish without running tests to save time.
Upgrade in a branch, review deprecation diagnostics, test dependencies and builds, then roll out with a rollback plan.
Change the version directly in production and ignore warnings.
questions.answer_key: Upgrade in a branch, review deprecation diagnostics, test dependencies and builds, then roll out with a rollback plan.
questions.explanation: Compatibility depends on compiler defaults, dependencies, editor tooling and the actual project runtime.

questions.prompt: Which statement is correct about “Gradual JavaScript-to-TypeScript Migration”?
options: The learner should publish hidden solutions so the exercise can grade itself.
The concept should be demonstrated with introducing typescript into existing projects and checked against its intended contract.
The safest approach is to skip diagnostics and trust the first output.
A type assertion automatically validates every value at runtime.
questions.answer_key: The concept should be demonstrated with introducing typescript into existing projects and checked against its intended contract.
questions.explanation: The supplied syllabus explicitly includes “Introducing TypeScript into existing projects”; connect it to a concrete example and verify the behavior relevant to this lesson.

questions.prompt: What is a good verification step after practicing “Gradual JavaScript-to-TypeScript Migration”?
options: Check migrating modules incrementally, include a meaningful failure case where appropriate, and document any runtime or version assumptions.
Assume prioritizing high-value type coverage is unnecessary because the code has type annotations.
Ignore compiler or test failures if the interface looks correct.
Treat passing a static token check as proof that the program executed correctly.
questions.answer_key: Check migrating modules incrementally, include a meaningful failure case where appropriate, and document any runtime or version assumptions.
questions.explanation: The syllabus includes “Migrating modules incrementally”. Verification should match the concept: type-level checks, runtime tests, configuration checks or human review as appropriate.
